main_body: A tall narrow vertical strip: a wooden post/rail on the left (x about 3-7) and three stacked repeated wooden blocks on the right, each with a small light square patch and brown plank face, separated by dark gaps and grey-blue end caps. It is drawn flat, front-on.
top_band: none. Column x=5 shows only dark runs (L=22) with transparent gaps; column x=8 shows a 1-row light highlight at rows 2-3, then brown face rows 4-14, with no multi-row lighter horizontal band above a distinct front face.
evidence: The drawing is three repeated vertical wooden panels or blocks beside a long vertical post, all seen face-on. The only lighter pixels are a 1-2 row highlight on each block, which is a rim or highlight and not a top surface. No horizontal beam or base shows a top face, so it is a front elevation and does not satisfy the 3/4 contract for a frame. It also does not read as a frame or rack, so the kind is questionable.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. It has about 4 wood steps (light tan, mid, brown, dark brown) and a few grain dots. Its dark edge pixels carry a brown tint (0% neutral), so the outline is tinted. There are no flat fills of 5x5 or larger. However, it is far thinner in colours and shading than the Beodeul references and reads as a repeated simple strip, so it is much lower in density.
